newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early trading.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks leap ahead in early trading.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks leaped to a new 1996 high on Friday morning on the back of futures-related buying and positive economic reports from the United States overnight, brokers said.
"Buying of blue chips, like HSBC up HK$2.50 at the open, seem to be related to the close of the September futures contract," said one broker with a European house.

The Hang Seng Index quickly moved up 115.54 points to 11,751.67, its highest intraday level this year. It later eased back to 11,727.84, up 91.71 points, after the first 30 minutes of trade. Turnover was an average HK$957 million.
The index's previous intraday high was 11,684.00, set on September 23.
The U.S. August durable goods report showing a slowdown in the U.S. economy, got mixed reviews on Wall Street, but was seen as non-inflationary in Hong Kong, brokers said.
They also cited the rally in bond prices as a positive factor affecting the local market.
"We have had yet another strong day in the long bond," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia.
The laggard commercial and industrial sector led the market in early trading, rising 0.85 percent in early trade.
The utility sector put on the next best performance.
HSBC was the most actively traded issue in terms of turnover and rose HK$2.50 at the open to touch an all-time high of HK$144.50 before falling back to trade at HK$142.50.
"Large overseas brokers were actively buying the shares in early trade, although volume was not particularly heavy," said one local broker.
The broker said the market appeared torn between active overseas buying and the cautious pre-holiday spirit of local players. Saturday is a public holiday in Hong Kong.
Sun Hung Kai Properties was also actively sought. The share leaped to a record high at the open, gaining HK$1.75 to HK$81.50, before falling back to trade HK$0.50 up at HK$80.25.
Henderson Land rose HK$0.50 at the open to HK$65.00, then eased HK$0.25 to HK$64.75.
Brokers pointed out that despite the company's recent share placement, the stock price had remained relatively firm, suggesting an optimistic outlook on the company and the Hong Kong property market.
Hong Kong Telecom rose HK$0.10 to HK$HK$13.60.
